The **Nebelwerfer** and the **A-10 Warthog's GAU-8 Avenger** are entirely different classes of weapon systems from different eras. They share a distinct circular or "revolving" visual appearance from the front, but they operate on completely opposite mechanical principles, calibers, and rates of fire. 

![](data:image/png;base64,)Wikipedia +1

The differences break down as follows:

### 📊 Direct Comparison

| Feature | [Nebelwerfer 41](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_cm_Nebelwerfer_41) (WWII) | [A-10 Warthog GAU-8 Avenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GAU-8_Avenger) (Modern) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Weapon Type** | Multiple Rocket Launcher (Stationary/Towed Artillery) | Gatling Gun (Rotary Aircraft Cannon) |
| **Caliber** | **158 mm** (Most common NbW 41 variant) | **30 mm** (30x173mm heavy rounds) |
| **Rate of Fire (RPM)** | ~4 to 6 rounds **per minute** (1 volley) | **3,900 rounds per minute** (Sustained) |
| **Action / Mechanism** | Static cluster of tubes; electrically ripple-fired sequentially. | Rotating barrel assembly; mechanically driven continuously. |
| **Ammunition Type** | Free-flight, spin-stabilized artillery rockets. | High-explosive incendiary (HEI) or Armor-piercing depleted uranium (API) cartridges. |

---

### 🔍 How They Differ

* **The "Revolving" Illusion:**
  + The **Nebelwerfer** does *not* rotate while firing. It is a stationary bundle of 5 or 6 barrel tubes. The circular arrangement is simply a space-efficient way to group the rocket tubes onto a lightweight carriage. The rockets are fired one by one in a rapid sequence (ripple-fired) to keep the recoil from overturning the launcher.
  + The **Warthog's GAU-8** is a true Gatling gun. The entire 7-barrel assembly actively spins at high speed. As it rotates, each barrel cycles through loading, firing, and extracting a cartridge in a continuous loop. 

    ![](data:image/png;base64,)Wikipedia +9
* **Caliber Size:**
  + The Nebelwerfer's "cartridge" is actually a massive rocket. At **158 mm to 300 mm**, it is a heavy artillery piece designed to level grid squares on a battlefield.
  + The GAU-8 fires a **30 mm** kinetic round—massive for an aircraft gun, but miniature compared to a rocket artillery projectile. 

    ![](data:image/png;base64,)Army.mil +4
* **RPM (Rate of Fire):**
  + The Nebelwerfer can empty its 6 pre-loaded tubes in about 10 seconds, but then the crew must manually reload it, limiting it to roughly **4 to 6 rounds per minute** over a sustained period.
  + The Warthog fires at an extreme **3,900 RPM**, meaning it shreds through nearly 70 rounds every single second. 

    ![](data:image/png;base64,)YouTube·Military History Visualized +2

The **Nebelwerfer's rocket bundle** and the **A-10 Warthog’s GAU-8 Gatling gun** share absolutely zero mechanical parts, design principles, calibers, or rates of fire. While both look like a giant revolving cylinder from the front, their core operations are completely opposite.

Here is exactly how their mechanisms, calibers, and RPMs differ:

### ⚙️ The Core Mechanism: Stationary vs. Spinning

* **Nebelwerfer (Static Cluster):** The six tubes **do not rotate** when firing. The cylinder stays completely still. The weapons are electrically fired one by one in a rapid sequence (ripple-fired) solely to keep the recoil from flipping the artillery carriage over.
* **A-10 Warthog GAU-8 (Rotary Cannon):** The entire 7-barrel assembly **actively spins at high speeds**. A hydraulic drive motor forces the barrels to rotate constantly. Every single barrel cycles through loading, locking, firing, and extracting a cartridge in a continuous mechanical loop.

### 📏 Caliber & Projectiles

* **Nebelwerfer:** It fires massive **158 mm to 300 mm spin-stabilized rockets**. These are self-propelled artillery pieces packed with high explosives or smoke compounds. There is no traditional brass "cartridge case" extracted; the entire rocket leaves the tube.
* **Warthog GAU-8:** It fires heavy **30 mm (30x173mm) ammunition**. These are traditional, massive kinetic cartridges with aluminum cases, firing either armor-piercing depleted uranium (API) or high-explosive incendiary (HEI) shells.

### ⏱️ RPM (Rate of Fire)

* **Nebelwerfer:** Fires **4 to 6 rounds per minute** under sustained combat. It can ripple-fire its 6 pre-loaded tubes in about 10 seconds, but then the crew has to manually pull out the spent rocket remnants and push heavy new rockets into the tubes from behind.
* **Warthog GAU-8:** Fires a blistering **3,900 rounds per minute**. It spits out roughly 65 to 70 heavy 30mm shells every single second, driven by a continuous linkless ammunition feed system that cycles empty cases right back into the drum.
